response.sql:
WITH pa AS (
  SELECT p.player_id, p.bats, AVG(b.double) AS avg_doubles
  FROM batting_postseason b
  JOIN player p ON p.player_id = b.player_id
  WHERE p.bats IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(p.bats) <> ''
  GROUP BY p.player_id, p.bats
),
idx AS (
  SELECT player_id, bats, avg_doubles,
         avg_doubles * 1.0 / (SELECT AVG(avg_doubles) FROM pa) AS idx
  FROM pa
),
final AS (
  SELECT player_id, bats, avg_doubles, idx,
         idx - AVG(idx) OVER (PARTITION BY bats) AS idx_minus_hand_avg
  FROM idx
)
SELECT player_id, bats, avg_doubles, idx AS index_value, idx_minus_hand_avg
FROM final
ORDER BY (idx_minus_hand_avg IS NULL), idx_minus_hand_avg DESC
LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: player.player_id is unique, so joining postseason batting records to player does not duplicate records.
Players whose postseason doubles are all NULL appear as rows with a NULL average. They are ignored by both the overall average and the hand averages, since AVG skips NULLs. They sort last.
A batting hand that is empty or only whitespace counts as empty and is excluded.
The overall average is the unweighted mean of the per-player averages, not the mean over all records. The hand average is the mean of the players' indexes within that hand.
